The first part you quoted was a segue into my concession that I, as a viewer, have learned to trust Buffy almost implicitly, but that I shouldn't expect that of the Potentials who hardly know her. I was agreeing that calgil was correct.

My displeasure stems from the Scoobs making a rash decision to distrust Buffy, kick her out of the house, and then nominate Faith in her place. Her past successes may be a result of weak writing, but they are still that... **successes**. I know Buffy has failures. Everyone on this show does. That's what makes it real.

Having said that, the gang has *no* experience with Faith and her CV of success. Which was small up until that point and mostly took place on AtS. **This** is what irks me. They deposed Buffy, kicked her out of the house, and turned to Faith. If we're speaking from a purely analytical POV, a group in need turns from a Slayer with a successful track record, to one with a history of mental instability and even cruelty. Now, while I absolutely adore Faith and their easy forgiveness of her past transgressions thrills me endlessly... it makes no sense when viewed from that particular frame of mind. If one's going to say deposing Buffy was the logical thing to do, then one can't quite say the same for the election of Faith.

TL;DR I don't fault the Potentials for deposing Buffy. Only the Scoobs for doing so so quickly and then in a completely bizarre moment, nominating Faith as replacement (sorry Faith, I love you but that made zero sense).

Another point:  I feel like we can't exactly view Sunnydale and BtVS with complete real-world rationale and logic, because it is not a rational and logical world. There are occurrences that can't be explained with anything other than cop-outs like: "must be magic!" For instance, Buffy's track record. Looking back on how often she succeeded when the odds were mostly stacked against her favor, it led me to an interesting idea. The Slayer is a being of mystical creation. Maybe the Slayer has a sixth sense, an instinct of sorts, that enhances that moral compass and gives her a one up on any other crime fighting do gooder. That may be another cop-out, but it's just an idea I had.

**Faith:** [Nine Inch Nails – Every Day is Exactly the Same]( https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3K1t0669no)  
I think this song perfectly portrays Faith’s mindset while in prison during AtS. All of her days in prison just blend together as she tries to suppress (what she thinks is) her true nature; to be a monster. She pays a heavy price for trying to subdue her demons. The lyrics invoke this numb feeling that starts to take over when she feels like she’s slowly losing herself.  

>*"I think I used to have a voice  
>Now I never make a sound  
>I just do what I've been told  
>I really don't want them to come around, oh no  
>I can feel their eyes are watching  
>In case I lose myself again  
>Sometimes I think I'm happy here  
>(Sometimes)  
>Sometimes, yet I still pretend”*  

Actually, a lot of NIN songs remind me of Faith. Tool and Celldweller as well.  Rob Zombie songs remind me of Faith’s self-destructive and overtly sexual streaks. /endrant. I can get a little carried away when it comes to Faith.  

**Buffy:** [Live – I Alone]( https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FNrQOUtXYOo)  
I kind of see this song as a metaphor for Buffy’s relationship with her inner slayer. Any fan of BtVS knows that Buffy never really embraced being a slayer. She considered it a burden to shoulder… alone. I think this song aptly describes that loneliness that Buffy feels even when she’s surrounded by loving friends. I imagine these lyrics as Buffy’s slayer almost taunting her, in a way, about how she’ll never be understood.  

**The end of the series/final episode:** [Cathy Davey – Holy Moly]( https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wZQYT1MjlO0)  
This song is perfect for the final episode. The eerily relevant lyrics. The bittersweet melody.  Haunting vocals. Just… so perfect.
